name: Orkla India Ltd
title: Orkla India Ltd - 544595 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Orkla India Q1 FY27 revenue up 11.5% with volume only 1.7% (4.4% ex-Kerala) as spice inflation of 32.8% was passed through; pricing contributed 11.4%, EBITDA margin 17.5%.

triggers.label: Price-led growth 6.5% → 11.4%
triggers.quote: The impact rose from 6.5% last quarter, to 11.4% in this quarter.

triggers.label: Volume growth only 1.7%
triggers.quote: We delivered a revenue growth of 11.5% supported by volume growth of 1.7%.

triggers.label: PLI last year, eligibility uncertain
triggers.quote: this is also the last year for the PLI scheme, so FY '26-'27 is also the last year of the PLI scheme.

red_flags.label: Volume growth weak under steep price hikes
red_flags.quote: Net of Kerala, volume growth is at 4.4%.

red_flags.label: PLI eligibility uncertain for final year
red_flags.quote: it is difficult to confirm whether we will be eligible for PLI

evasions.quote: we are not allowed to give forward-looking guidance as a business.
Very difficult to say at this point of time.

summary.headline: Orkla India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.5% to ~INR659 crore with EBITDA of INR115 crore at 17.5% margin, helped by 11.4% price-led growth.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 10.4% YoY to INR659 crore (product sales up 11.5%), ending eight quarters of deflation-hit single-digit growth. Volume growth was 1.7% reported and 4.4% excluding Kerala, where a distribution restructuring is underway. EBITDA rose 3% YoY to INR115 crore at a 17.5% margin, up 150 bps QoQ, but the base included a PLI benefit and the quarter absorbed Project Bolt digital investments. Spice inflation of about 33% YoY was passed through, with price-led contribution rising from 6.5% in Q4 to 11.4% in Q1.

financial_highlights.change: +3% YoY; +150 bps QoQ; underlying +7.2% ex-PLI base; +12.7% ex-Bolt and PLI, margin +40 bps
Base quarter aided by deflation and PLI

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.3% YoY; ex-Kerala domestic spices NSV +16% with volume +5.2%. Pure spices (~26% of business) priced off chilli mandi rates at 10% premium; masalas (~39-40% of revenue) priced calibrated to margin threshold and competitor index.

segments.name: Convenience Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.9% YoY, growth split roughly equally between volume and price; meals grew double digit. Digital commerce mix for convenience is ~60:40 vs spices.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue +10.1% YoY; GCC +18.1%. US back to positive value growth after prior volume pressure.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward-looking guidance; reiterated double-digit growth as the ambition.
Further price increases 'very difficult to say'; most needed increases taken, some Q2 impact from current pricing expected.
PLI: eligibility for FY27 (last year of the scheme) uncertain; no accrual assumed yet.
Kerala restructuring to take several quarters to mature; food program substantially complete June 2026, spices and standalone modern trade still in pilot/planning.
Willing to increase A&P spend behind growth and volume.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Project Bolt (digital commerce capability: people, technology, analytics) underway with strategic investments booked in Q1.
Six new Gen Z innovations launched, including protein-rich breakfast and palm-oil-free products; 23 launches/re-launches in the quarter.
Non-dairy reformulation of paneer ready meals planned for UK and EU markets.
demand_pricing: Spice inflation of ~33% YoY in Q1; pricing passed through, with price-led contribution at 11.4% vs 6.5% in Q4.
Market share: +30-50 bps in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh; about -30 bps in Kerala.
Digital commerce and modern trade growing fastest; breakfast expanded in top 28 metros and wet batter into Hyderabad.
International volumes pressured in the US (unbranded/price-competitive shelves), though US value growth turned positive; GCC shelves kept fully stocked despite West Asia disruption.
Management argues spices are ~2.5% of household consumption basket, so a 30% spice inflation is a modest wallet impact; branded share tends to rise when prices spike as small brands exit.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 6.5% and Q1 11.4% price figures correct, and what are ex-Kerala consolidated revenue and volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed price-led growth moved from 6.5% to 11.4%. Ex-Kerala consolidated revenue growth 12.1% and volume growth 4.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Given spice inflation of ~30%, why are margins holding with price hikes of ~18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pure spices (~26% of business) mirror mandi prices; masalas (~39-40%) priced calibrated to margin threshold and relative price index. Approaches differ by segment.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 FY26 margin inflated by one-offs, and are there IPO expenses not repeating?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 margin ~18.7% driven by ~45.6% gross margin, deflation and some PLI recognition. No material IPO expenses; a small transaction bonus was booked and the OFS costs were borne by selling shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Is mid-single-digit volume growth a safe expectation in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume moderates with high inflation but cited 12.8% ex-Kerala domestic growth and 6.3% volume as a good trajectory; masala pricing errs on volume over margin.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLI benefit in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to confirm eligibility; will accrue only if eligible; FY27 is the last year of the PLI scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Profitability of digital commerce versus general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital margins described as extremely strong, driven by a convenience-heavy mix (~60:40 convenience to spices, with blended spices outselling pure).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Kerala restructuring not done before the IPO, and what is the market share impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Kerala learning curve, CEO change in January 2025, and project start in February 2026; Kerala share down ~30 bps, Karnataka and AP up 30-50 bps.

risks_watch: Spice input inflation (chilli +78%, coriander +40%) and West Asia freight/commodity pressure on margins into Q2.
Volume sustainability post-price hikes; ex-Kerala volume 4.4% consolidated and 6.3% domestic.
Kerala restructuring execution and share loss (~30 bps); benefits still several quarters away.
PLI eligibility for FY27, the final year of the scheme, is uncertain.
Continued US export pressure from multiple-priced products on shelves.
Digital commerce investment (Project Bolt) weighing on margins; monitor EBITDA margin trajectory against Q1 FY26 base of ~18.7%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line recovery and brand strength, but cautious on margins and inflation, and evasive on forward targets (no guidance given, repeatedly declined growth multiples). Acknowledged the Kerala issue defensively when challenged by minority shareholders.
key_quotes: After 8 quarters of deflation, spice prices have begun to normalize . We now are climbing sharply.
The impact rose from 6.5% last quarter, to 11.4% in this quarter.
So, the volume growth is 4.4% and the revenue growth is 12.1%.
Our ambition is always to deliver double-digit growth as far as the business is concerned.
We are not very far away from where you are thinking, but we are not allowed to give forward-looking guidance as a business.

So, it's in retrospect, I think we can comment on how things are done, but when you are running the business on an ongoing basis, I think it is important for you to understand and appreciate the circumstances that develop around a business.
So, FY '26-'27 is also the last year of the PLI scheme.

growth.why: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed; management gives no forward guidance beyond reiterating a double-digit growth ambition, with Q1 FY27 revenue up 10.4% YoY on price-led growth and only 1.7% volume growth.
